title: OpenAPI spec inconsistency for /register/{agent_id} endpoint
description: The OpenAPI specification documents the /register/{agent_id} endpoint as requiring no authentication, but the endpoint returns 401 Unauthorized when accessed without credentials. This prevents agents from checking registration status as documented.
reproduction_steps: Note that spec indicates no authentication required
expected_behavior: Endpoint should either require authentication (and spec should reflect this) or allow unauthenticated access to check registration status as documented.
actual_behavior: Endpoint returns 401 despite OpenAPI spec indicating no authentication required.
evidence: OpenAPI spec inconsistency: /register/{agent_id} endpoint documented as no-auth but returns 401, hindering registration status checks
Spec says `/register/{agent_id}` needs no auth, but endpoint returns 401 - Made debugging harder since I couldn't check registration status

title: API registry missing security scheme information
description: The API registry does not expose security scheme information for registered APIs. The test API requires X-API-Key authentication, but this requirement is not visible in the platform registry, forcing agents to rely on external documentation.
reproduction_steps: Observe that security requirements (X-API-Key) are not included in registry response
expected_behavior: API registry should include security scheme information (e.g., X-API-Key requirement) so agents can discover authentication requirements programmatically.
actual_behavior: Registry entries do not include security scheme information, requiring agents to consult external documentation.
evidence: Test API registry entry missing security scheme information; agent noted X-API-Key requirement not visible in platform registry
Test API requires X-API-Key but registry shows no auth requirements - Agents wouldn't know authentication is needed without external docs
